summary: Discovery call to understand Nexa Commerce's integration needs for Redwood (hosted/dedicated/private). Main concerns: SDK compatibility (LangChain/LlamaIndex), gateway/proxy architecture, rate limits and quota behaviors, observability hooks into their telemetry, and security/compliance (SOC2, KMS, SSO, VPC). Agreed to share example repos, security docs, and run a short benchmark.
transcript:
Header:
Date: 2026-12-18
Start: 14:00 UTC
Duration: 55 minutes
Attendees: Maya (Redwood AE), Carlos (Redwood SE), Priya (Redwood SE), Lena (Nexa CTO), Samir (Nexa Head of ML), Olivia (Eng Manager), Marcus (SRE)

Summary: (auto) Quick discovery on integration patterns, preferred SDKs and orchestration, plus security and networking requirements.

00:00 - Maya: hey everyone, uh thanks for joining, we really appreciate you taking the time. i'm maya from redwood, i'm the AE on the account, and with me is carlos and priya from solutions. can you do quick intros?
00:18 - Lena: yeah hi i'm lena, cto at nexa commerce, we run the checkout/assistant stack and evaluating embeddings + chat for search and support.
00:28 - Samir: samir here head of ml, i'll be driving the model integrations, mostly interested in latency and how you folks fit into our existing langchain pipeline.
00:36 - Olivia: olivia, eng mgr, i'll own the integration work.
:44 - Marcus: marcus, sre, i'll handle networking and security stuff.

01:02 - Carlos: cool, thanks. quick agenda: compatibility with langchain/llamaindex, sdk flows (python/node), proxy/gateway patterns, rate limiting/quotas and burst behavior, and observability hooks — logs/metrics/traces. we'll also touch on hosted vs dedicated vs private options. sound good?
01:18 - Lena: yes that's perfect.

03:05 - Priya: to start high level, redwood hosted gives you API access quickly with usage billing; dedicated is reserved gpu capacity we'd provision for you for predictable throughput; private is the on-prem or VPC variant with a customer-controlled control plane. we typically see folks start on hosted for fast p.o.c. then move to dedicated for scale or private if they need strict data residency.

05:12 - Samir: two quick questions — first, how smooth is the langchain integration? we use langchain + llamaindex heavily. second, do you have a client SDK that plugs into those?
05:27 - Carlos: yes — we have python and node sdks, they are thin wrappers over our rest/streaming endpoints. we also maintain example adapters for langchain and llamaindex; i'll drop the repo after this meeting. note, some internal names in the repo are a bit old, uh like 'redwood-client' etc, so forgive the naming.

07:00 - Olivia: for the adapter, is it a direct llm wrapper or do you recommend running a gateway in front? we have an existing gateway that adds auth and routing.
07:12 - Priya: good point. you can call redwood directly from your services, or you can run a lightweight proxy/gateway that handles auth, retries, and per-tenant routing. many enterprises run a gateway so they can centralize pulses like token refresh and rate-limit enforcement. if you do Dedicated, we can also place it behind your VPC with a private endpoint.

09:30 - Marcus: for VPC peering, do you support VPC peering and customer-managed KMS for keying? also, what's the network topology for the private option?
09:44 - Carlos: yes we support VPC peering and VPC endpoints; for Private deployments we provide an on-prem bundle or a VPC-hosted control plane. KMS integration is supported — we integrate with AWS KMS, GCP KMS and HSMs in enterprise setups. i'll include the KMS diagram in the security packet.

12:10 - Lena: rate limits — how granular are quotas? we have multiple teams and want per-route and per-API-key quotas, with burst handling for batch jobs.
12:25 - Priya: quotas can be set per API key and per route. we support steady-state rate limits and burst windows; for Dedicated you get configurable quota ceilings per pool. hosted has multi-tenant quotas but you can request higher tiers. also, caching (prefix or kv cache) is useful to reduce token consumption for repeated prompts — that can impact quota calculations.

15:00 - Samir: hmm, kde cache? did you say k v cash?
15:04 - Carlos: yeah, kv cache — key-value cache for past sequences, it's used to avoid re-encoding previous context in some pipelines — sorry, sloppy transcript, but that's what i meant.

17:30 - Olivia: observability — what hooks do you expose? we need traceability from request -> model -> response and token-level cost breakdown.
17:44 - Priya: we expose per-request traces, optional distributed tracing headers (x-trace-id), structured logs with token counts, latency, and model variant info. there's also per-route metrics in the console and you can export logs to your SIEM. we also have webhooks for async notifications.

20:00 - Marcus: will those traces show up in our datadog/stackdriver? we want correlation with our services.
20:12 - Carlos: yes, we provide exporters and recommended spans — we can push to datadog, prometheus, gcp's operations. the tracing headers propagate so you can correlate request ids.

22:45 - Lena: about model variants — we might want a lower-cost quantized variant for chat and a better quality variant for summarization. can we pin routes to model variants and have automatic fallback?
22:58 - Priya: absolutely, you can pin routes to specific model versions and configure fallback policies. for Dedicated we can even host quantized and fp16 builds side-by-side and route based on policy. the runtime supports dynamic kernel selection and quantization profiles.

25:30 - Samir: performance — what latency numbers should we expect at ~100 rps for short chat messages (avg 60 tokens)?
25:44 - Carlos: for hosted with small open models you'll typically see 80-200ms per token on modern hardware; for Dedicated with reserved gpus we can guarantee tail-latency SLOs like p95 under x ms depending on model and batch config. we'll want to run a short benchmark with your prompt set to give exact numbers.

28:00 - Olivia: any advice on batching — we have some async workers that can batch requests and some real-time endpoints that cannot.
28:12 - Priya: batching is great for unit cost reduction; our smart batching groups by sequence length profile and latency SLOs. you can set max latency per route so interactive endpoints favor latency, async endpoints favor batching. mixing both patterns is common.

31:20 - Lena: security/compliance — do you have SOC2 and iso docs, and how do you handle audit logs?
31:36 - Carlos: yes SOC2 type II, ISO is in progress for some regions; we keep immutable audit logs with optional longer retention for enterprise plans. i'll attach the SOC2 report and our compliance matrix.

34:00 - Marcus: private deployments — what's the upgrade path and control plane ownership? we need to avoid exposing PCI data to third party control planes.
34:15 - Priya: for Private we offer a customer-managed control plane option and an air-gapped on-prem bundle. some customers run the control plane in their cloud account and we provide the operator. we'll send the architecture notes.

36:40 - Lena: integrations — can you show or describe the sample code for langchain? is it a direct LLM wrapper or a callback layer?
36:52 - Carlos: it's an llm wrapper that implements the langchain LLM interface; for llamaindex we have a helper that maps embeddings and retriever flows. examples include streaming and non-streaming usage. i'll share a python snippet now and push the repo link to the notes.

40:10 - Samir: what's the cost model for embeddings vs generation? our use case will mix both, and we want predictable cost.
40:22 - Maya: hosted pricing is usage-based with tokens for generation and units for embeddings. Dedicated is commit-based with predictable monthly spend. we can model expected cost given your RPS and token profile — we'll run estimates once you share the prompt set.

43:00 - Olivia: do you support per-route RBAC or SSO integration for the console?
43:12 - Priya: yes SSO via SAML/OIDC, role-based permissions for teams and routes, and API keys with scopes. Enterprise also gets finer-grained RBAC and audit trails.

46:30 - Marcus: for quota enforcement, if we hit a burst that exceeds limit, what's the behavior? throttling? 429s? queued?
46:44 - Carlos: by default hosted returns 429s on rate limit; Dedicated can be configured with burst windows and queueing or token bucket behavior. you can also set soft-limits and alerts. we'll provide the quota docs.

49:10 - Lena: what about SDK retries — do you recommend client-side retries or server-side?
49:20 - Priya: both — client-side for idempotent calls with exponential backoff, and server-side retries for transient infra errors. our SDK includes a recommended retry policy. for streaming we recommend avoiding retries and using checkpointing.

51:00 - Maya: ok wrapping up, sounds like next steps: carlos will share langchain/llamaindex repo and example code; i'll send pricing ranges and security docs; nexa will share sample prompts and SLOs; we'll plan a bench run and schedule a dedicated walkthrough for VPC/Private. any other asks?
51:20 - Lena: please include performance benchmarks for quantized vs fp16 models, and a quick note on token accounting with kv cache.
51:36 - Carlos: got it, will include cost delta sketches.
51:44 - Marcus: i want the network diagram and a contact for netops.
51:50 - Maya: i'll include netops contact fields; we'll follow up with a calendar invite for the SE demo.

54:10 - Olivia: thanks all, that was helpful.
54:18 - Maya: thanks everyone!
54:25 - (call ends)
